unit_index.interpretation: Hecke diagonalization is a perspective-selection mechanism: it chooses a basis compatible with all multiplicative correspondences. In that basis, symmetry in the geometric domain becomes arithmetic factorization in the coefficient domain.

unit_index.source_title: Notes on the Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: A plausible proof architecture combines hidden family structure, positivity, a global Euler proxy, and Fourier-complex analysis
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The unspecified global Euler proxy is the central proposed bridge between prime-local data and analytic continuation; the positivity pairing would convert that structure into a zero-location constraint.
unit_index.interpretation: The list is a synthesis of proof burdens rather than a sequence of lemmas. Each ingredient repairs a different failure: family structure supplies relations, positivity supplies sign control, the proxy preserves local arithmetic globally, and Fourier-complex analysis mediates the representations.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: Deformation in a family turns inaccessible individual L-functions into statistical objects
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Reframe family formation as a controlled change of question—from an isolated L-function to a deformable statistical object—and distinguish the information retained at low zeros from the information forgotten by high-zero universality, without importing later conductor ordering or local-measure machinery.
unit_index.interpretation: Because the source says that number fields have no formal general notion of family, its parameter-map proposal is pragmatic: it turns automorphic forms that can be deformed and isolated together into an ensemble on which averaging can address both collective behavior and otherwise inaccessible individual questions. This gains analytic tractability while limiting the working definition to parametrized families that arise with usable methods. The low-versus-high-zero contrast further suggests that family formation can remain visible near the central point even when high scaled spacings obey a universal law.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: Persistent central zeros and functional-equation parity require independent family refinements
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The next-order coefficient tF(p) and the ramification polynomial M(w) are independent bridge objects for rank and root-number statistics.
unit_index.interpretation: Leading local equidistribution, next-order bias, and ramified parity encode different information channels. Treating them separately prevents a central atom or sign imbalance from being mistaken for a different bulk symmetry.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: The identity orbital term creates Plancherel mass and all other orbits control the error
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The functorial pushforward of unramified Plancherel measure is the bridge from spectral counting on H to Satake statistics on GLn.
unit_index.interpretation: The trace formula is a decomposition of signal and error: identity geometry becomes statistical law, and control of other conjugacy classes determines how far the law can be transferred into simultaneous prime averages.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: Natural trace-formula weights can manufacture a misleading symmetry type
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Treat weighted and unweighted averaging as different probability measures and use that distinction to diagnose why a trace-formula output cannot by itself identify the counting-family symmetry type.
unit_index.interpretation: The Petersson trace formula naturally accesses a weighted family measure, not the desired unweighted counting measure. In this spin family the representation-theoretic data fix essential symplectic type, yet the available weighted low-zero statistic appears inconsistent with the unweighted prediction. Thus weighting is a live confound: if the conjecturally identified central-value weight fluctuates with the zeros, changing measure can change the observed density without changing the underlying spin representation. The trace formula gains analytic access but loses direct identification of the unweighted estimand; removing the weights is the unresolved test.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: A Plancherel-null local condition defeats the trace formula before symmetry can be tested
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Plancherel volume is the bridge between a local constraint and trace-formula countability; zero volume breaks the bridge.
unit_index.interpretation: Trace-formula equidistribution begins with a nonzero identity-term mass. A null condition removes that main term, so ordinary limit multiplicity cannot distinguish the desired family from the spectral background.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: A critical center would force a symplectic pairing, excluding regular algebraic orthogonal forms
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The conjectural motive and its l-adic realization are the bridge between Deligne criticality and the automorphic symmetric/exterior-square classification.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof transports one binary invariant—pairing sign—through motivic, l-adic, and automorphic representations. Criticality constrains parity tightly enough that the transported sign becomes incompatible.
